prompt:
The `vcfa-deployment-sync` project talks to a VCF Automation appliance in VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1. Its client is a stub. Implement it.

VCF Automation publishes no OpenAPI document, so the wire format this project codes against was transcribed by hand from the VCF Automation xAPIs reference pages at developer.broadcom.com. The result is in `docs/contract.json`, and every page it came from is recorded in `docs/official_sources.json`. Read the contract before you write anything: it pins the paths, the field names, the requiredness flags, the pagination defaults and the wire rules this project holds itself to. Three operations are in scope.

| operation | method | path |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `exchangeRefreshToken` | POST | `/csp/gateway/am/api/login/oauth` |
| `listDeployments` | GET | `/deployment/api/deployments` |
| `patchDeployment` | PATCH | `/deployment/api/deployments/{deploymentId}` |

Fill in `src/com/broadcom/vcfa/VcfAutomationClient.java`, which is the only file you need to change. `Json.java` is a provided JSON reader/writer, and the files under `harness/` and `docs/` are fixed; the verifier restores all of them from pristine copies before it compiles, so editing them cannot change the outcome.

**Paging across an expiring token.** `listAllDeployments(pageSize)` returns every deployment in server order, with none dropped and none duplicated. The appliance issues a short-lived access token, and it will expire partway through the paging run: the Deployment API answers 401 for the request that hits the expiry. Recover from that without throwing away the pages you already have. Exchange the refresh token for a new access token, replay only the request that was rejected, and carry on from there — pages already fetched must not be requested a second time. Obtain a token before the first Deployment API call, then reuse it rather than re-authenticating on every call, and stop paging as soon as the response envelope says the current page is the last one.

**Unset fields are absent, not empty.** `updateDeployment(deploymentId, name, description, iconId)` takes null for any field the caller is not changing. A field the caller did not set is left out of the JSON body entirely; it is never sent as `""` or as `null`. The same rule governs the token exchange: it carries the grant type, a state value and the refresh token, and none of the other optional fields the reference lists for that operation.

Run `./verify.sh`. It compiles the project, runs the test harness against a loopback mock pinned to the contract, and checks the traffic it recorded. The mock's request log lands in `run/requests.jsonl` with the exact method, path, query string, `Authorization` header and raw body of every call, which is the fastest way to see what actually went over the wire. A JDK and `python3` are on PATH; nothing is downloaded and no VMware endpoint is contacted.
